page: Amazon Web Services g5.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance optimized for graphics-intensive applications and machine learning workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro System, the instance features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It supplies 96 vCPUs derived from 48 dedicated physical cores with multithreading support, operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The hardware package bundles four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs providing an aggregate of 89 GB of VRAM. System memory consists of 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided through a bundled 3800 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional acceleration for generative AI and graphics pipelines. The quad-A10G configuration places the instance in the top tier across LLM inference benchmarks, processing 9212.26 tokens per second for small model prompts, 2836.73 tokens per second for 7B models, and 397.89 tokens per second on large 70B models. Text generation throughput reaches 88.36 tokens per second on 7B parameters. The system also delivers strong performance in specialized graphics and computation tasks, scoring 77514.0 in Geekbench ray tracing and achieving top-tier results in PassMark CPU encryption at 101561.54 points. In-memory data structures benefit from 79.8 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and strong small-block cached read throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on raw single-core computational limitations. The AMD EPYC processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 753.39, falling into the bottom 10%, while single-core Geekbench performance sits at an average 1310.0. The architecture lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions, relying on standard AVX, AES, and FMA instructions. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is moderate at 120.08 GB/sec. From a resource efficiency standpoint, the dense packaging of four discrete GPUs, high vCPU capacity, and 3.8 TB of NVMe storage delivers high throughput per node for multi-GPU inference, rendering, and video processing, while representing an overprovisioned profile for strictly CPU-bound serial tasks.

The g5.24xlarge is suitable for distributed LLM inference, real-time ray tracing, cloud workstations, video encoding pipelines, and parallelized compilation workloads utilizing Clang. Its large memory footprint and fast NVMe storage also accommodate high-throughput caching and mid-tier deep learning model training.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by a 3.3 GHz AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. It bundles four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs totaling 89 GB of VRAM, 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 50 Gbps network interface. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in LLM prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and 70B parameter models, alongside strong Geekbench ray tracing and PassMark encryption scores. While single-thread CPU performance is lower than modern compute-focused alternatives, the aggregated GPU capacity and NVMe throughput make it an efficient platform for machine learning inference, graphics rendering, Clang compilation, and high-concurrency caching services.
